metadata.title: Micah
metadata.subtitle: Micah 1:1 – 7:20 (21 questions)
metadata.description: Questions on the Book of Micah according to the King James Version (1769).
metadata.author: King James Version (1769)

questions.text: How does Micah 1:3-4 describe the LORD coming forth to judgment?

options.text: The LORD cometh in a thick cloud and speaketh from the hills unto the people
The LORD treadeth upon high places, and the mountains are molten under him
The LORD sendeth angels of destruction to lay waste the cities of the land
The LORD appeareth in a chariot of fire and shaketh the pillars of earth

questions.text: What does Micah 1:5 name as the transgression of Jacob and high places of Judah?

options.text: The heathen nations and their abominable idolatrous groves on the hills
The desolation of the holy temple and the ceasing of all morning sacrifices
Samaria for Jacob's transgression, and Jerusalem for Judah's high places
The contempt of the priesthood and the breaking of the solemn statutes

questions.text: How far does the incurable wound reach according to Micah 1:9?

options.text: Unto the border of Edom and throughout the wide barren desert
Unto distant Egypt and unto the great rushing waters of the river
Unto the banks of Jordan and unto the coast of the salt sea
Unto Judah, unto the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem

questions.text: What transgression does Micah 2:1-2 denounce?

options.text: They devise iniquity upon their beds and covet fields and take them away
They withhold tithes and defraud the holy house of appointed oblations
They sacrifice upon high places and worship lifeless idols of wood
They sell the poor into bondage and drive the fatherless from the gate

questions.text: What do the adversaries say unto the prophets in Micah 2:6?

options.text: Prophesy unto us of peace and gladness, for that will do us good
Prophesy not! They shall not prophesy to them, that they take not shame
Prophesy only within the temple, and keep silence in the open streets
Prophesy unto the rulers and princes, but leave the people at peace

questions.text: What promise is given in Micah 2:13 for the remnant of Israel?

options.text: An angel from heaven shall deliver them from captivity and guide them
A faithful shepherd shall pasture them and gather them upon holy Zion
The breaker is come up before them, and the LORD on the head of them
A wise prophet shall lead them and build them an habitation of rest

questions.text: With what image does Micah 3:2-3 charge the princes of the house of Israel?

options.text: They cast the needy into dark pits and leave them without food
They eat up the standing corn and leave no cluster for the poor
They beat the righteous with rods and spoil them of their heritage
They flay their skin from off them and chop them as for the pot

questions.text: How does Micah 3:5 expose the false prophets?

options.text: They cry peace to him that feedeth them, but prepare war against others
They prophesy by night in secret and hide themselves from open daylight
They proclaim continual destruction and curse all that honor them not
They flatter the wealthy for filthy lucre and keep silence before kings

questions.text: What word of judgment does Micah 3:12 pronounce upon Zion and Jerusalem?

options.text: Zion shall stand for ever, and the holy sanctuary shall never fall
Zion shall be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps
A new temple shall be built, and the holy city shall rule all lands
Zion shall be kept by mighty angels, and no enemy shall enter her gates

questions.text: What does Micah 4:1 foresee for the last days?

options.text: The nations shall forsake Zion, and the holy mount shall be desolate
The mount of the LORD shall sink down, and the people wander scattered
The mountain of the house of the LORD shall be established in the top
An earthly ruler shall erect an exceeding strong fortress upon Ephraim

questions.text: How is the peace of the nations described in Micah 4:3-4?

options.text: They cast their armor into the deep sea and build walls about gates
They fashion spears into bolts and set bars of iron upon their towers
They purchase weapons of war and maintain peaceful trade with neighbours
They beat their swords into plowshares and sit under their own vine

questions.text: Whither must the daughter of Zion go before she is delivered (Micah 4:10)?

options.text: Go forth out of the city into the field, even to Babylon, to be delivered
Into the wilderness of Judah, where she may abide safely from enemies
Down into Egypt, to find refuge and bread in the midst of fierce famine
Unto the heights of mount Carmel, to build a new sanctuary unto God

questions.text: Which place is promised in Micah 5:2 as the origin of the ruler in Israel?

options.text: Hebron in the hill
Beth-lehem Ephratah
Shiloh in Ephraim
Gibeah in Benjamin

questions.text: How is the ministry of the ruler described in Micah 5:4?

options.text: He shall serve as high priest and purge the altar from all past guilt
He shall rule with a sharp sword and destroy all adversaries from earth
He shall stand and feed in the strength and majesty of the name of the LORD
He shall remain hidden in secret and be known only unto the humble

questions.text: By what two similes does Micah 5:7-8 describe the remnant of Jacob?

options.text: As an eagle in heaven and as a faithful shepherd over his sheep
As the stars of the sky and as the fine sand upon the sea shore
As a consuming fire and as an overflowing tempest in the plains
As a dew from the LORD and as a young lion among flocks of sheep

questions.text: To what does the LORD call his people in Micah 6:1-3?

options.text: To contend before the mountains: O my people, what have I done unto thee?
To bring costly burnt offerings, that the LORD may be reconciled to them
To weep in sackcloth and ashes, that the fierce anger of God may cease
To wage battle against the heathen, that the promised land may be saved

questions.text: What doth the LORD require of man according to Micah 6:8?

options.text: To offer ten thousands of rivers of oil and to fast continually
To do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God
To pay all prescribed tithes and keep solemn assemblies without fail
To make long prayers in the temple and instruct youth in statutes

questions.text: What sins are condemned by the LORD in Micah 6:10-16?

options.text: Heathen altars upon the mountains and idolatrous groves in the land
Neglect of the holy altar and profaning the appointed feast days
Treasures of wickedness, the scant measure, and keeping the statutes of Omri
Perverting judgment by false witness and taking gifts of bribery

questions.text: How does the prophet mourn over the society in Micah 7:2?

options.text: The holy sanctuary is burned, and the priests are fled far away
The fruitful land is laid waste, and no man gathereth the vintage
The fenced walls are overthrown, and foreign armies fill the gates
The good man is perished out of the earth: they all lie in wait for blood

questions.text: What does the prophet speak against his enemy in Micah 7:8?

options.text: Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise
Tremble, O mine enemy: for my God shall suddenly overthrow thee
Depart from me, O mine enemy: for I shall never be moved in the way
Bow down before me, O mine enemy: for my strength shall prevail

questions.text: With what praise does the Book of Micah conclude (Micah 7:18-19)?

options.text: The LORD is King for ever, and his throne shall endure unto all ages
Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity, casting sins into sea?
The LORD is my shepherd in the earth, and I shall never be destitute
The LORD will deliver his chosen heritage and bring them from Babylon
